title: Getting started
text: MAGMA.Celltyping software package facilitates conducting cell-type-specific enrichment tests GWAS summary statistics.

title: Getting started
text: Specify want large files downloaded . NOTE: Make sure change storage_dir somewhere tempdir() want make sure results aren’t deleted R session closes!
code: storage_dir <- tempdir()

title: Getting started
text: need summary statistics file analyse input. example, can download UK Biobank summary statistics ‘fluid_intelligence’ using get_example_gwas(). provide pre-munged version file.

title: Getting started
text: lab created MungeSumstats, robust Bioconductor package formatting multiple types summary statistics files. highly recommend processing GWAS summary statistics MungeSumstats continuing. See full_workflow vignette details. minimum info needed munging : - “SNP”, “CHR”, “BP” first three columns. - least one columns: “Z”,“”,“BETA”,“LOG_ODDS”,“SIGNED_SUMSTAT”
code: path_formatted <- MAGMA.Celltyping::get_example_gwas(   trait = "prospective_memory")

title: Getting started
text: Note can input genome build summary statistics step can inferred left NULL:
code: genesOutPath <- MAGMA.Celltyping::map_snps_to_genes(   path_formatted = path_formatted,   genome_build = "GRCh37")

title: Getting started
text: Rather preprocessing GWAS , can instead use MAGMA_Files_Public database created. contains pre-computed MAGMA SNP--genes mapping files hundreds GWAS. can browse GWAS traits available looking provided metadata.csv file.
code: magma_dirs <- MAGMA.Celltyping::import_magma_files(ids = "ieu-a-298") ## Using built-in example files: ieu-a-298.tsv.gz.35UP.10DOWN ## Returning MAGMA directories.

title: Getting started
text: ewceData provides number CellTypeDatasets (CTD) used cell-type transcriptomic signature reference files. want create single-cell transcriptomic reference, ’ll need first convert CTD using instructions found EWCE package documentation . Note cell type dataset loaded code Karolinksa cortex/hippocampus data . full Karolinska dataset hypothalamus midbrain instead use following: DRONC seq AIBS datasets use:
code: ctd <- ewceData::ctd() ## see ?ewceData and browseVignettes('ewceData') for documentation ## loading from cache ctd <- MAGMA.Celltyping::get_ctd("ctd_allKI") ctd <- get_ctd("ctd_Tasic") ctd <- get_ctd("ctd_DivSeq") ctd <- get_ctd("ctd_AIBS") ctd <- get_ctd("ctd_DRONC_human") ctd <- get_ctd("ctd_DRONC_mouse") ctd <- get_ctd("ctd_BlueLake2018_FrontalCortexOnly") ctd <- get_ctd("ctd_BlueLake2018_VisualCortexOnly") ctd <- get_ctd("ctd_Saunders")

title: Getting started
text: MAGMA.Celltyping offers suite functions conducting various types cell-type-specific enrichment tests GWAS summary statistics. celltype_associations_pipeline wraps several functions previous versions MAGMA.Celltyping set run separately. include: Linear enrichment: calculate_celltype_associations(EnrichmentMode = "linear") internally. Activated run_linear=TRUE. Top 10% enrichment: Uses calculate_celltype_associations(EnrichmentMode = "Top 10%") internally. Activated run_top10=TRUE. Conditional enrichment: Uses calculate_conditional_celltype_associations internally. Activated run_conditional=TRUE. Thus, celltype_associations_pipeline designed make analyses easier run. ’ve also saved pre-computed version results dataset:
code: MAGMA_results <- MAGMA.Celltyping::celltype_associations_pipeline(   magma_dirs = magma_dirs,   ctd = ctd,   ctd_species = "mouse",    ctd_name = "Zeisel2015",    run_linear = TRUE,    run_top10 = TRUE) MAGMA_results <- MAGMA.Celltyping::enrichment_results

title: Getting started
text: merge_results imports MAGMA enrichment results files merges one can easily plotted analysed.
code: merged_results <- MAGMA.Celltyping::merge_results(   MAGMA_results = MAGMA_results) ## Saving full merged results to ==> /tmp/RtmpiTiKA6/MAGMA_celltyping./.lvl1.csv knitr::kable(merged_results)

title: Getting started
text: Now ’ll construct heatmap visualizing enrichment results, GWAS shown y-axis cell-type shown x-axis. Results can facetted kind test run (linear, top10%, /conditional).
code: heat <- MAGMA.Celltyping::results_heatmap(   merged_results = merged_results,    title = "Alzheimer's Disease (ieu-a-298) vs.\nnervous system cell-types (Zeisel2015)",   fdr_thresh = 1) ## 14 results @ FDR < 1

title: Getting started
text: Now can also plot p-value results (-log10 p-values) based significance threshold (either linear top10%) together bar plot (sorted top10% results).
code: barplot_ggplot <- MAGMA.Celltyping::results_barplot(   merged_results = merged_results,   title="Alzheimer's Disease (ieu-a-298) vs.\nnervous system cell-types (Zeisel2015)",   fdr_thresh = 1,   horz_line_p = .2 ) ## 14 results @ FDR < 1

title: Getting started
text: Get phenotypes greatest number significant cell-type enrichment results.
code: top_phenos <- merged_results %>%    dplyr::group_by(EnrichmentMode, GWAS) %>%   dplyr::summarise(Celltype=dplyr::n_distinct(Celltype)) %>%   dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(Celltype)) ## `summarise()` has grouped output by 'EnrichmentMode'. You can override using ## the `.groups` argument. knitr::kable(top_phenos)

title: Getting started
text: Get phenotypes-celltype enrichment results significant p-values (per phenotype).
code: top_enrich <- merged_results %>%    dplyr::group_by(EnrichmentMode, GWAS) %>%   dplyr::slice_min(FDR, n = 2) knitr::kable(top_enrich)

title: Full workflow
text: MAGMA.Celltyping software package facilitates conducting cell-type-specific enrichment tests GWAS summary statistics. following vignette shows step--step version MAGMA.Celltyping pipeline. newer streamlined version pipeline (wraps many functions), please see Getting Started vignette.

title: Full workflow
text: need GWAS summary statistics file analyse input. example, can download UK Biobank summary statistics ‘fluid_intelligence’ using get_example_gwas().
code: gwas_sumstats_path <- MAGMA.Celltyping::get_example_gwas(   trait = "fluid_intelligence",   munged = FALSE)

title: Full workflow
text: lab created robust Bioconductor package formatting multiple types summary statistics files: MungeSumstats (please cite associated publication use package): Murphy, Schilder, & Skene, MungeSumstats: Bioconductor package standardization quality control many GWAS summary statistics, Bioinformatics, Volume 37, Issue 23, 1 December 2021, Pages 4593–4596, https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btab665 use MungeSumstats reformat summary statistics Fluid Intelligence. minimum info needed munging : SNP, CHR, BP first three columns. least one columns: (“Z”,“”,“BETA”,“LOG_ODDS”,“SIGNED_SUMSTAT”) Genome builds: UK Biobank data Ben Neale uses “GRCh37” specify . However, don’t know genome build GWAS sum stats , MungeSumstats infer information default (simply set ref_genome=NULL). sake example, also provide pre-munged version file. use , can skip previous two steps.
code: path_formatted <- MungeSumstats::format_sumstats(path=gwas_sumstats_path,                                                  save_path = tempfile(fileext = ".formatted.tsv.gz"),                                                  ref_genome ="GRCh37") path_formatted_intelligence <- MAGMA.Celltyping::get_example_gwas(     trait = "fluid_intelligence",      munged = TRUE)

title: Full workflow
text: Next, must convert GWAS summary statistics file gene-level signature can compare gene-level transcriptomic cell-type reference. Note can input genome build summary statistics step can inferred left NULL:
code: genesOutPath_intelligence <- MAGMA.Celltyping::map_snps_to_genes(     path_formatted = gwas_sumstats_path,     genome_build = "GRCh37")

title: Full workflow
text: second step MAGMA.Celltyping prepare Cell Type Dataset (CTD) reference, get gene signatures cell-type reference. ewceData package comes CTD use example. want import single cell RNA-seq dataset, needs converting CTD format; please see EWCE vingette explanation . Note cell type dataset loaded code Karolinksa cortex/hippocampus data . full Karolinska dataset hypothalamus midbrain instead use following: can find list datasets provided package using ?MAGMA.Celltyping::get_ctd:
code: ctd <- ewceData::ctd() ctd <- MAGMA.Celltyping::get_ctd("ctd_allKI") ctd <- get_ctd("ctd_Tasic") ctd <- get_ctd("ctd_DivSeq") ctd <- get_ctd("ctd_AIBS") ctd <- get_ctd("ctd_DRONC_human") ctd <- get_ctd("ctd_DRONC_mouse") ctd <- get_ctd("ctd_BlueLake2018_FrontalCortexOnly") ctd <- get_ctd("ctd_BlueLake2018_VisualCortexOnly") ctd <- get_ctd("ctd_Saunders") ctd <- get_ctd("ctd_Zeisel2018")

title: Full workflow
text: Preparing quantiles CTD now something automatically handled MAGMA.Celltyping user doesn’t need pre-step anymore. However, still export function prepare_quantile_groups case users want control. prepare_quantile_groups calculates quantile groups celltype within single-cell dataset. single-cell dataset mouse, change ctd_species argument.
code: ctd <- MAGMA.Celltyping::prepare_quantile_groups(ctd = ctd,                                                  ctd_species="mouse") # Examine how the quantile groups look print(ctd[[1]]$specificity_quantiles[c("Gfap","Dlg4","Aif1"),]) print(table(ctd[[1]]$specificity_quantiles[,1]))

what: Run the main cell type association analysis
title: Full workflow
text: analyses can run either linear top10% enrichment modes. advantages/disadvantages. Linear mode: Performs linear regression analysis using continuous gene-association scores GWAS MAGMA results continuous specificity scores cell-type CTD reference. mode takes advantage gene-level weights order get accurate association estimates. However, mode also tends give significant results general, may capturing signatures multiple cell-types . Top 10% mode: Performs gene-set enrichment analysis (GSEA) using top 10% cell-type-specific genes cell-type (.e. genes top specificity decile). Unlike linear mode, top 10% mode discards gene-level weight data testing instead treats genes categorical data (gene list gene list). lose nuance gene-level weights, potential capture less cell-type signatures given test (due using handful top genes), can make interpretation easier. Let’s start linear: Now let’s add top 10% mode plot linear together top 10% mode.
